FINDINGS:

Fractures:
None.

Joint alignment:
Normal.

Degenerative changes:
Focal high to full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral femoral condyle and tibia posteriorly. This is most likely related to a prior osteochondral injury.

Mild cartilage loss in the patellofemoral cartilage with thinning of the patellar cartilage inferiorly.

Bone marrow signal:
Normal. Subchondral cysts involving the lateral tibial plateau.

Anterior cruciate ligament: Mild signal abnormality involving the ACL ligament at the posterior insertion to the femur, likely related to a mild sprain.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Normal.
Medial collateral ligament: Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: The fibular collateral ligament, IT band and biceps femoris are intact. Signal abnormality involving the popliteus tendon insertion at the lateral femoral condyle, most likely tendinosis. The popliteomeniscal fascicles are not well seen and likely torn, with associated mild medial displacement of the popliteus tendon below the popliteus hiatus.

Medial meniscus: Normal.
Lateral meniscus: Complex multidirectional tear involving the posterior, body and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is volume loss in the body and a large displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. There is complete loss of tissue in the posterior horn, likely a complete radial tear. There is unusual U shaped fragment adjacent to the posterior root ligament.

Extensor mechanism: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Normal.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Normal.

Joint effusion: Small to moderate right knee joint effusion, with synovial thickening. There is a small loose body in the suprapatellar recess measuring approximately 3 mm.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Complex multidirectional tear of the body, posterior and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, with a large unusually shaped displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. Recommend an orthopedic surgery consultation.
*Mild signal abnormality of the ACL, likely from a sprain, without evidence of tear.
*Focal high to full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral compartment posteriorly, most significantly the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 2 & 1/2 years of knee pain after ATV accident. Pain at the anterior and posterior aspects. Associated buckling. Difficulty with knee extension. No prior surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Focal marrow edema with cyst formation at the posterior medial tibial plateau subjacent to the PCL attachment. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness fissuring with subchondral edema at the peripheral aspect of the lateral trochlea. Chondral heterogeneity at the median ridge with small focal full-thickness fissuring.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Patellofemoral chondrosis.
2.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear.
3.	Focal marrow edema at the posterior medial tibial plateau with cystic change may represent intraosseous ganglion cyst formation.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion. There is significant soft tissue swelling surrounding the knee.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is thickening and increased signal involving the distal posterior cruciate ligament with partial tear (approximately 50% of the fibers) of the posterior medial fibers. There is mild thickening and increased signal involving the proximal and mid aspect of the PCL.

There is complete radial tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is unremarkable.

There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament with distal avulsion of the superficial component which is retracted proximally and superficial to the pes anserine tendons compatible with a pseudoStener lesion. There is also high-grade injury involving the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial component of the MCL with thickening of the posterior oblique ligament.

There is almost complete tear of the lateral collateral ligament at its femoral attachment. There are thinned out fibers that appear physically continuous. This is likely a functionally complete tear. There is also almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon as it courses around the lateral femoral condyle with significant thinning and laxity of the tendon. There is disruption of the popliteal fibular ligament. The distal biceps femoris insertion remains intact.

There is significant bone marrow edema at the posterior tibial plateau fractures. There is also bone contusion involving the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and minimal contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an enchondroma in the distal femur.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL with a moderate grade injury of the PCL.

2. High-grade injury involving the medial collateral ligament including distal avulsion of the superficial MCL with pseudo Stener lesion.

3. High-grade tear of the lateral collateral ligament which is likely functionally complete.

4. Almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon. Injury to the popliteal fibular ligament.

5. Complete radial tear involving the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.

6. Significant bone marrow edema surrounding the known tibial plateau fracture with a bone contusion in the lateral femoral condyle.

7. large knee joint effusion.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Osseous contusions involving the sulcus terminalis and posterolateral tibial plateau as well as the posterior medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete tear of the midsubstance.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Low grade 2 sprain pattern with partial tear of the deep fibers.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Recent pivot shift contusions with complete rupture of the midsubstance of the ACL and low grade 2 sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia derecha.
Hallazgos:
Formación quística subcortical del aspecto anterior del platillo tibial medial de 7 x 6 mm en sus
ejes mayores, sin significado patológico específico.
No hay otras alteraciones de señal de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos impresionan de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales. Cartílago
troclear sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial del cartílago rotuliano su faceta
lateral sin cambios óseos secundarios.
Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano.
Tendones cuadricipital, la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
Aumento de señal de la inserción proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la rótula.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, hallazgo inespecífico, podría
representar fenómenos de mal alineamiento rotuliano.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
